summary: Specifies IANA guidelines for allocating new values for the Routing Type field in the IPv6 Routing Header. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5871 sets rules for assigning new values to the IPv6 Routing Header's Routing Type field. It requires IETF Review or IESG Approval and notes two values already available for experiments.

questions: how to get a new routing type
how are ipv6 routing types allocated
what is the ipv6 routing header registry policy
which routing type values are for experiments
subtitle: IANA allocation rules for IPv6 Routing Header type values.

tldr.problem: The IPv6 Routing Header's Routing Type field had no IANA allocation guidance.
tldr.mechanism: New Routing Type values are allocated through IETF Review or IESG Approval, following the procedures in RFC 5226.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5871 updates RFC 2460 and notes that values 253 and 254 are available for experimental use.

today: RFC 5871 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 2460. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: A Rule for Routing Types
sections.content: The IPv6 Routing Header includes a Routing Type field. Before this document, there was no IANA guidance for allocating new values for that field. RFC 5871 supplies the missing allocation rules and updates the IPv6 specification in RFC 2460.
sections.plainLanguage: The Routing Type field needed a rule for assigning new values. This RFC provides that rule.

sections.title: Review Before Assignment
sections.content: New Routing Type values are allocated through IETF Review or IESG Approval, as defined in RFC 5226. The RFC also notes that experimental values 253 and 254 are available for use under RFC 4727.
sections.plainLanguage: A new value needs IETF review or IESG approval. The RFC identifies 253 and 254 as experimental values.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 5871 does not change the security properties of the Routing Header. It notes that past experience shows it is easy to design routing headers with significant problems.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC does not change Routing Header security. It cautions that routing headers can be designed in ways that cause significant problems.
